mechanism_narrative: A sustained quarterly rise in GDP growth (GDPC1) signals robust economic expansion, boosting corporate earnings and equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth exceeds median but S&P 500 20d returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in a baseline comparison.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% triggers heightened labor market confidence, strengthening corporate profits and equity valuations, resulting in positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% in the next month
failure_condition: UNRATE crosses below 5.0% but S&P 500 5d returns fail to be statistically positive (p > 0.05) in a regime-specific test.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in GDP growth (GDPC1) and decline in federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1.5% signals accommodative monetary policy and robust demand, amplifying equity valuations and generating positive 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >5% and FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5% in the next month
failure_condition: Both proxies move as expected, but S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a regime-conditional test.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 signals weakening supply-side growth, compressing margins and driving negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 105.0 in the late-cycle expansion regime
failure_condition: INDPRO crosses below 105.0 in late-cycle periods but S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a regime-specific test.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in PCE inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2.0% signals deflationary pressures, lowering real interest rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL remains below 2.0% for 6 months but S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) compared to a baseline of similar inflation trends.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in household demand (HOUST) above 1500 units triggers increased consumer spending, driving corporate profits and equity valuations higher, resulting in positive 5-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises above 1500 in the next month
failure_condition: HOUST crosses above 1500 but S&P 500 5d returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) in a regime-specific test.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent rises in GDP growth (GDPC1) and labor participation (PAYEMS) signal robust economic expansion, strengthening corporate earnings and equity valuations, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >5% and PAYEMS rises by >2% in the next month
failure_condition: Both proxies move as expected, but S&P 500 20d returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) in a regime-conditional test.

mechanism_narrative: In a recessionary environment, a decline in business investment demand (RSAFS) below 500 million dollars signals weak corporate activity, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls below 500 in the recessionary regime
failure_condition: RSAFS crosses below 500 in recessionary periods but S&P 500 60d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) in a regime-specific test.
